page: Amazon Web Services c8ib.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance configuration provides two dedicated vCPUs mapped to a single physical core with hyperthreading enabled at a base clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system includes 4.0 GB of high-speed 7 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding 2.0 GB per core, along with an L3 cache capacity of 480 MB. It also incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). There is no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage, and baseline network performance is rated at 2 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate contrasting performance characteristics across workloads. Single-threaded compression tasks show exceptional execution, with gzip compression reaching 33.81 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 14.37 GB/sec, placing both in the top 25 percent. In contrast, overall multi-core compute throughput reflects the physical single-core limit, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 2153.47 and PassMark CPU scoring 4058.96. Memory read-only uncached throughput measures 23.9 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 15.85 GB/sec. Low-footprint language model evaluation indicates small-model prompt processing at 322.26 tokens per second and text generation at 77.73 tokens per second.

Qualitatively, c8ib.large serves as an accessible entry point to modern Intel Xeon Gen8 compute architecture. By coupling a high clock frequency with modern vector and matrix extensions in an entry-level tier, it avoids the expense of larger resource allocations. The trade-offs include constrained total memory capacity, lack of local disk storage, and throughput ceilings tied to the single physical execution core.

The instance is best suited for compute-focused single-threaded tasks, compression and decompression pipelines, lightweight background batch processing, and microservices requiring modern instruction set acceleration.

It is paired with 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing a standard 1:2 compute-optimized memory-to-vCPU ratio. The Nitro-backed virtual machine does not include bundled local storage and provides a 2 Gbps baseline network throughput. Hardware acceleration capabilities include AVX-512 and Intel AMX instructions. Benchmark testing highlights strong single-threaded data compression and decompression performance alongside moderate small-model inference generation. However, multi-core throughput, raw memory bandwidth, and static web serving capacities remain constrained by the single-core allocation. Qualitatively, c8ib.large functions as an economical tier for accessing modern instruction sets, fitting lightweight batch processing, compression pipelines, and single-threaded compute workloads.
